@graph.headline: The AI Model Routing Guide: Which Model for Which Agent (Q2 2026 Edition)
@graph.description: Architectural guide to dynamic model routing: balancing latency, token economics, and reasoning depth across production AI applications.
@graph.keywords: ai model routing, llm gateway architecture, cost optimization llm, semantic routing, hybrid model deployment
@graph.abstract: Production AI systems cannot rely on a single monolithic foundation model. By implementing dynamic semantic routing, engineering teams direct simple queries to ultra-fast lightweight models while escalating multi-step reasoning to frontier reasoning architectures. This hybrid pattern slashes API costs by up to 78 percent while improving response speeds.

acceptedAnswer.text: An architectural pattern where incoming user requests are analyzed and dispatched to the most suitable model based on complexity, latency, and cost.

mainEntity.name: How does semantic classification work in routing?

acceptedAnswer.text: A small embeddings model or lightweight classifier categorizes intent in under 15 milliseconds before selecting the optimal downstream LLM.

mainEntity.name: What cost savings are achievable with model routing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Production deployments typically achieve a 60 to 80 percent reduction in token spend compared to sending all traffic to top-tier reasoning models.

mainEntity.name: How do you handle model provider outages?

acceptedAnswer.text: Modern gateways include automated fallback cascades that reroute traffic to secondary providers if error rates or latencies spike.

mainEntity.name: What open-source tools facilitate LLM routing?

acceptedAnswer.text: LiteLLM, OpenRouter, Cloudflare AI Gateway, and custom Fastify middleware provide battle-tested routing and caching layers.
